messages.subject: Download png from interactive plots
parts:
I am having a hard time understanding how to download png from shiny server.

can anybody please reply how to use downloadhandler() code for plotly, dygraph and highcharters.

library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)

ui<-dashboardPage(
    dashboardHeader(),
    dashboardSidebar(disable = TRUE),
    dashboardBody(
    downloadButton('down','click me'),
    plotOutput('ab')
    
    ))


server<-function(input,output){
sample<-reactive({plot(iris)})    

output$ab<-renderPlot(sample())
    
 output$down<- downloadHandler(
     'FUB.png',
     content = function(file){
        png(file)
        print(sample())
        dev.off()
     }
     )

}

shinyApp(ui,server)

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: Download png from interactive plots
parts:
When plot() runs, it writes a png to disk; it does not return an object that can be printed (which is what you're trying to do). In more technical terms, the png is written as a side effect of running plot().

It happens that renderPlot will capture that png file and send it to the browser. However, when you try to run sample() again in your downloadHandler, it will not write a png to disk.

If you use ggplot() instead of plot(), it does return a printable object, so that would work. Another possibility is to move the plotting code out to a function, and call it from both the renderPlot() and from the downloadHandler callback. You would want to write the function so that any input values would be passed to it, as in myPlot(input$x, input$y).

-Winston
